services: Construction & infrastructure: differing site conditions / REAs
Bonding & certified payroll on large awards
final_text:
Hello Jimmy,

I hope you are having a great week. My name is Marcos Gonzalez and I am the Managing Attorney at GovSpring Legal, where we help federal contractors keep evolving regulations from slowing down operations. I have been following B&H's utility rehabilitation work for the National Park Service at Rocky Mountain National Park, and with the project still early in its lifecycle, I wanted to check in on how performance is going. High-elevation water and sewer work over aging, decades-old systems tends to include subsurface conditions that don't match the as-builts, and that is exactly where the differing-site-conditions clause and a well-documented request for equitable adjustment can protect your schedule and your margin. We also help contractors keep their bonding, certified-payroll, and compliance programs clean on awards of this size, so a contracting officer's questions never slow the build down.

I would love to introduce myself and see how we might support B&H as the work ramps up. Let me know if you would like to discuss any legal issues, free of charge. I'm available next week, and you can schedule a call here or call me at (202) 407-3556. You can also read more about my associate and I on our webpage.

I have CC'd my associate and my law clerk, who would also participate in any scheduled call.

Warmly,
Marcos Gonzalez
